body:
## Pull request overview

This PR implements an Airtable-style calendar view component for displaying records as events with Month, Week, and Day view modes. The implementation follows the Object UI architecture by providing both a base UI component and a schema-driven renderer that maps data fields to calendar events.

**Changes:**
- Added `CalendarView` UI component with navigation controls and three view modes
- Created schema-driven renderer with flexible field mapping and color coding support
- Added documentation and playground examples

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 7 out of 7 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/calendar-view.tsx` | Schema-driven renderer with field mapping and action callbacks |

| `docs/components/calendar-view.md` | Component documentation with usage examples and API reference |
| `docs/spec/component-library.md` | Added calendar-view to component library spec |
| `apps/playground/src/data/examples.ts` | Added calendar-view example with sample event data |
</details>

These field name mappings lack JSDoc comments explaining their purpose. According to Rule #3 (Schema First Mindset), every property in the Schema MUST have JSDoc to enable auto-generation of documentation.

Both 'view' and 'defaultView' properties serve the same purpose, creating redundancy. The inputs array at lines 156-168 also defines both. Consider using only one property name for clarity.
```suggestion
        view={schema.view || 'month'}
```
Removed the redundant `defaultView` property and updated the code to use only `view` with improved label and description. See commit 4f7d2ea.
Added JSDoc comments to all field name mappings (titleField, startDateField, endDateField, colorField, allDayField) for auto-documentation generation. See commit 4f7d2ea.
